title: apricity serve --link: Link peer, /link WebSocket clock stream and ping, custom.apricity.link in amplify_outputs.json
description:
## Intent
`apricity serve --link`: one Link peer in the server, a clock WebSocket, and the advertisement. Makes apricitus-79d979 green.

## Steps
1. `crates/apricity-cli/src/main.rs`, `Cmd::Serve`: `--link` ("Join the Link session and offer its clock to the web app at /link").
2. `crates/apricity-cli/src/serve.rs`: when linked, a `Session` (M2) owned by the app state; route `GET /link` upgrading to a WebSocket (axum's `ws` feature; note the Cargo change in the log); send `clock` on connect, on change and every 250 ms; answer `ping` with `pong`; answer anything else with `error` and keep streaming; never pass anything to the session. Without `--link`, `/link` is 404 with the message.
3. `amplify_outputs.json`: `custom.apricity.link.url` only when linked.
4. `scripts/serve-smoke.sh`: open `/link`, read one clock message, ping once.

## Verify
`cargo test -p apricity-cli serve` (the serve scenarios green) and `scripts/serve-smoke.sh`.

Commit: `feat(<this task id>): serve --link clock stream`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
